newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialists put jobs at centre of campaign.
newsitem.headline: French Socialists put jobs at centre of campaign.

text.p: France's Socialist party said on Monday it planned to put unemployment at the centre of its campaign ahead of the second round of a parliamentary election next Sunday.
A first round vote on Sunday showed the combined left narrowly ahead of the ruling centre-right UDF/RPR coalition.

Socialist economic policy-maker Dominique Strauss-Kahn said the left's first round victory was a big rejection of the centre-right, but said that he did not think French people had been completely convinced by Socialist policies.
"We have work to do this week to show them that things can indeed change," he said.

Asked about the economic policies which the party would push this week, he said: "Jobs, jobs, jobs. All the proposals we are making are centred on employment. There are other issues in French society which are worth considering, but employment and purchasing power are at the heart of it," he said.
France's high unemployment, running at a record 12.8 percent, has been seen as a major reason for the centre-right's poor first-round showing on Sunday.
Strauss-Kahn also reiterated that the Socialists would preserve and favour the existing universal pensions system.
The Socialists have said they would repeal a law passed earlier this year introducing private pension funds, which are meant to complement the existing pensions system.
